\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{അപമാനം} (apamānaṁ)}{അപമാനം (apamānaṁ)}]{\ml{അപമാനം} (apamānaṁ) — humiliation; an insult}

\label{lesson:ML-C524-apamanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for petty spite, then the Malayalam for to admire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{അപമാനം}}
\textbf{\ml{അപമാനം}} — \emph{apamānaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}humiliation; an insult\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{എല്ലാവരുടെയും} \ml{മുന്നിൽ} \ml{വഴക്ക്} \ml{കേട്ടത്} \ml{അവന്} \ml{അപമാനമായി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ellāvaruṭeyuṁ munnil vaḻakkŭ kēṭṭatŭ avanŭ apamānamāyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Being scolded in front of everyone was a humiliation for him.
\end{quote}

\ml{അപമാനിക്കുക} is to insult; \ml{അപ}- away + \ml{മാനം} honour.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{അപമാനം}} (\emph{apamānaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{apamāna}, \textquotedblleft{}disrespect, disgrace\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 433).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apamānaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apamānaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ellāvaruṭeyuṁ munnil vaḻakkŭ kēṭṭatŭ avanŭ apamānamāyi.} — Being scolded in front of everyone was a humiliation for him.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for petty spite, then the Malayalam for to admire, then say \emph{apamānaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{അപമാനം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Humiliation; an insult\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക} (uṟṟunōkkuka)}{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക (uṟṟunōkkuka)}]{\ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക} (uṟṟunōkkuka) — to stare}

\label{lesson:ML-C524-urrunokkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to admire, then the Malayalam for humiliation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക}} — \emph{uṟṟunōkkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to stare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പുതിയ} \ml{കുട്ടിയെ} \ml{ക്ലാസിലെ} \ml{എല്ലാവരും} \ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{putiya kuṭṭiye klāsile ellāvaruṁ uṟṟunōkki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone in the class stared at the new child.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കി}, \emph{uṟṟunōkki}.

\ml{ഉറ്റ്} closely + \ml{നോക്കുക} to look.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക}} (\emph{uṟṟunōkkuka}) is native Dravidian, a compound of \ml{ഉറ്റ്}, \textquotedblleft{}near, closely\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 710), and \ml{നോക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to look\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3794).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟṟunōkkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uṟṟunōkkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{putiya kuṭṭiye klāsile ellāvaruṁ uṟṟunōkki.} — Everyone in the class stared at the new child.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to admire, then the Malayalam for humiliation, then say \emph{uṟṟunōkkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കുറ്റബോധം} (kuṟṟabōdhaṁ)}{കുറ്റബോധം (kuṟṟabōdhaṁ)}]{\ml{കുറ്റബോധം} (kuṟṟabōdhaṁ) — guilt; a guilty conscience}

\label{lesson:ML-C524-kurrabodham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for humiliation, then the Malayalam for to stare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കുറ്റബോധം}}
\textbf{\ml{കുറ്റബോധം}} — \emph{kuṟṟabōdhaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}guilt; a guilty conscience\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അമ്മയോട്} \ml{നുണ} \ml{പറഞ്ഞതിൽ} \ml{അവൾക്ക്} \ml{കുറ്റബോധം} \ml{തോന്നി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ammayōṭŭ nuṇa paṟaññatil avaḷkkŭ kuṟṟabōdhaṁ tōnni.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She felt guilty about lying to her mother.
\end{quote}

\ml{കുറ്റം} a fault + \ml{ബോധം} awareness: knowing one has done wrong.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കുറ്റബോധം}} (\emph{kuṟṟabōdhaṁ}) is a Malayalam compound built from \ml{കുറ്റം}, \textquotedblleft{}a fault\textquotedblright{}, a native word (DEDR 1851), and Sanskrit \emph{bodha}, \textquotedblleft{}consciousness, awareness\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṟṟabōdhaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuṟṟabōdhaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ammayōṭŭ nuṇa paṟaññatil avaḷkkŭ kuṟṟabōdhaṁ tōnni.} — She felt guilty about lying to her mother.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for humiliation, then the Malayalam for to stare, then say \emph{kuṟṟabōdhaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക} (āścaryappeṭuka)}{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക (āścaryappeṭuka)}]{\ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക} (āścaryappeṭuka) — to be surprised; to marvel}

\label{lesson:ML-C524-ascaryappetuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to stare, then the Malayalam for guilt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക}} — \emph{āścaryappeṭuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to be surprised; to marvel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മകന്റെ} \ml{മാർക്ക്} \ml{കണ്ട്} \ml{അച്ഛൻ} \ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെട്ടു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{makanṟe mārkkŭ kaṇṭŭ acchan āścaryappeṭṭu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father was surprised to see his son's marks.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെട്ടു}, \emph{āścaryappeṭṭu}.

\ml{ആശ്ചര്യം} surprise + \ml{പെടുക}; \ml{അത്ഭുതപ്പെടുക} says nearly the same.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക}} (\emph{āścaryappeṭuka}) is built from \ml{ആശ്ചര്യം}, from Sanskrit \emph{āścarya}, \textquotedblleft{}wonderful, a marvel\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1464), and the native helper verb \ml{പെടുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āścaryappeṭuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āścaryappeṭuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{makanṟe mārkkŭ kaṇṭŭ acchan āścaryappeṭṭu.} — Father was surprised to see his son's marks.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to stare, then the Malayalam for guilt, then say \emph{āścaryappeṭuka} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വേവലാതി} (vēvalāti)}{വേവലാതി (vēvalāti)}]{\ml{വേവലാതി} (vēvalāti) — fretting; agitation}

\label{lesson:ML-C524-vevalati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for guilt, then the Malayalam for to be surprised.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വേവലാതി}}
\textbf{\ml{വേവലാതി}} — \emph{vēvalāti} — \textquotedblleft{}fretting; agitation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മകൾ} \ml{വൈകിയപ്പോൾ} \ml{അമ്മ} \ml{വേവലാതിയോടെ} \ml{കാത്തിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{makaḷ vaikiyappōḷ amma vēvalātiyōṭe kāttirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When her daughter was late, Mother waited in a fret.
\end{quote}

Spoken; \ml{വേവലാതിപ്പെടുക} is to fret, to worry oneself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വേവലാതി}} (\emph{vēvalāti}) is a spoken word; no source we can open explains it, so its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vēvalāti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vēvalāti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{makaḷ vaikiyappōḷ amma vēvalātiyōṭe kāttirunnu.} — When her daughter was late, Mother waited in a fret.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for guilt, then the Malayalam for to be surprised, then say \emph{vēvalāti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വേവലാതി} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fretting; agitation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Words for what you lived and felt}

\label{lesson:ML-R524-review-517-524}



\begin{quote}
Say the Malayalam for an emotion and delight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an emotion, delight, to bellow, wrath, to be upset
  \item dread, to feel ashamed, loneliness, to long for, bliss
  \item anxiety, self-respect, to be astonished, tender affection, to grumble
  \item compassion, sympathy, to throb, unease, to sob
  \item satisfaction, melancholy, to smile, nostalgia, to sigh
  \item curiosity, impatience, to get angry, freshness, to get fed up
  \item a state of mind, a grudge, to mutter, petty spite, to admire
  \item humiliation, to stare, guilt, to be surprised, fretting
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An emotion? (\textbf{\ml{വികാരം}}, \emph{vikāraṁ}.) Delight? (\textbf{\ml{ആഹ്ലാദം}}, \emph{āhlādaṁ}.) To bellow? (\textbf{\ml{അലറുക}}, \emph{alaṟuka}.) Wrath? (\textbf{\ml{കോപം}}, \emph{kōpaṁ}.) To be upset? (\textbf{\ml{വിഷമിക്കുക}}, \emph{viṣamikkuka}.) Dread? (\textbf{\ml{ഭയം}}, \emph{bhayaṁ}.) To feel ashamed? (\textbf{\ml{ലജ്ജിക്കുക}}, \emph{lajjikkuka}.) Loneliness? (\textbf{\ml{ഏകാന്തത}}, \emph{ēkāntata}.) To long for? (\textbf{\ml{കൊതിക്കുക}}, \emph{kotikkuka}.) Bliss? (\textbf{\ml{ആനന്ദം}}, \emph{ānandaṁ}.) Anxiety? (\textbf{\ml{ഉത്കണ്ഠ}}, \emph{utkaṇṭha}.) Self-respect? (\textbf{\ml{ആത്മാഭിമാനം}}, \emph{ātmābhimānaṁ}.) To be astonished? (\textbf{\ml{അമ്പരക്കുക}}, \emph{amparakkuka}.) Tender affection? (\textbf{\ml{വാത്സല്യം}}, \emph{vātsalyaṁ}.) To grumble? (\textbf{\ml{മുറുമുറുക്കുക}}, \emph{muṟumuṟukkuka}.) Compassion? (\textbf{\ml{അനുകമ്പ}}, \emph{anukampa}.) Sympathy? (\textbf{\ml{സഹതാപം}}, \emph{sahatāpaṁ}.) To throb? (\textbf{\ml{വിങ്ങുക}}, \emph{viṅṅuka}.) Unease? (\textbf{\ml{അസ്വസ്ഥത}}, \emph{asvasthata}.) To sob? (\textbf{\ml{വിതുമ്പുക}}, \emph{vitumpuka}.) Satisfaction? (\textbf{\ml{സംതൃപ്തി}}, \emph{saṁtṛpti}.) Melancholy? (\textbf{\ml{വിഷാദം}}, \emph{viṣādaṁ}.) To smile? (\textbf{\ml{പുഞ്ചിരിക്കുക}}, \emph{puñcirikkuka}.) Nostalgia? (\textbf{\ml{ഗൃഹാതുരത്വം}}, \emph{gṛhāturatvaṁ}.) To sigh? (\textbf{\ml{നെടുവീർപ്പിടുക}}, \emph{neṭuvīrppiṭuka}.) Curiosity? (\textbf{\ml{ജിജ്ഞാസ}}, \emph{jijñāsa}.) Impatience? (\textbf{\ml{അക്ഷമ}}, \emph{akṣama}.) To get angry? (\textbf{\ml{ദേഷ്യപ്പെടുക}}, \emph{dēṣyappeṭuka}.) Freshness? (\textbf{\ml{ഉന്മേഷം}}, \emph{unmēṣaṁ}.) To get fed up? (\textbf{\ml{മടുക്കുക}}, \emph{maṭukkuka}.) A state of mind? (\textbf{\ml{മാനസികാവസ്ഥ}}, \emph{mānasikāvastha}.) A grudge? (\textbf{\ml{പക}}, \emph{paka}.) To mutter? (\textbf{\ml{പിറുപിറുക്കുക}}, \emph{piṟupiṟukkuka}.) Petty spite? (\textbf{\ml{കുശുമ്പ്}}, \emph{kuśumpŭ}.) To admire? (\textbf{\ml{ആരാധിക്കുക}}, \emph{ārādhikkuka}.) Humiliation? (\textbf{\ml{അപമാനം}}, \emph{apamānaṁ}.) To stare? (\textbf{\ml{ഉറ്റുനോക്കുക}}, \emph{uṟṟunōkkuka}.) Guilt? (\textbf{\ml{കുറ്റബോധം}}, \emph{kuṟṟabōdhaṁ}.) To be surprised? (\textbf{\ml{ആശ്ചര്യപ്പെടുക}}, \emph{āścaryappeṭuka}.) Fretting? (\textbf{\ml{വേവലാതി}}, \emph{vēvalāti}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
